lessons.title: Projects, programs and operations
lessons.description:
A **project** is a temporary effort to create a unique result. It has a start, an end and a defined goal — unlike **operations**, which keep the business running day to day.

- A **program** groups related projects so their benefits are managed together.
- A **portfolio** is everything an organization invests in, prioritised against its strategy.

Knowing which one you are running tells you how to plan it and who decides.

lessons.title: The triple constraint
lessons.description:
Every project balances **scope**, **time** and **cost** — and quality depends on all three.

1. Add scope and you need more time or money.
2. Cut the budget and something else has to give.
3. Shorten the schedule and cost or risk goes up.

A good project manager makes these trade-offs visible early, so sponsors decide with open eyes.

lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

questions.explanation: Opening a branch is temporary and unique.

questions.prompt: The sponsor adds features but keeps the deadline. What usually has to change?
questions.explanation: More scope in the same time needs more resources.

lessons.title: Work breakdown structure
lessons.description:
A **work breakdown structure (WBS)** splits the project into deliverables, then into smaller work packages you can estimate and assign.

- Break work down until a package takes roughly one to two weeks.
- Name deliverables as nouns ("Training manual"), not tasks.
- Every package has one owner.

If it is not in the WBS, it is not in the project.

lessons.title: Schedules and the critical path
lessons.description:
Link work packages by their dependencies and you get a network. The **critical path** is the longest chain through it — any delay on it delays the whole project.

- Tasks off the critical path have **float**: they can slip a little.
- Watch the critical path weekly; that is where your attention pays off.

courses.title: Agile and Scrum in Practice
courses.description: Agile and Scrum in Practice — part of Apex Training Institute's Project & Business programs.
courses.shortDescription: Project management, agile delivery and business skills.

lessons.title: Why agile
lessons.description:
Agile teams deliver in **short iterations** and learn from real feedback instead of predicting everything up front.

It suits work where requirements change or are hard to know in advance — software, new services, process improvement.

lessons.title: The Scrum framework
lessons.description:
Scrum organises work into **sprints** of one to four weeks.

- **Product owner** — orders the backlog by value.
- **Scrum master** — removes obstacles and protects the process.
- **Developers** — build the increment.

Each sprint has planning, a daily stand-up, a review with stakeholders and a retrospective.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: Scrum
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

lessons.title: User stories and estimation
lessons.description:
A **user story** describes value from the user's point of view: *"As a customer, I want to reset my PIN so I can use my card again."*

Teams estimate stories in relative **story points** and use their **velocity** — points finished per sprint — to forecast.

lessons.title: Kanban boards
lessons.description:
A Kanban board shows work moving through columns such as **To do → Doing → Review → Done**.

Limit **work in progress** in each column: finishing beats starting.

lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

courses.title: Excel for Data Analysis
courses.description: Excel for Data Analysis — part of Apex Training Institute's Data & Technology programs.

lessons.title: Tables, not ranges
lessons.description:
Turn raw data into an Excel **Table** (Ctrl + T) before you analyse it.

- Headers stay visible and formulas fill down automatically.
- New rows are picked up by charts and pivot tables.
- Structured references like `[@Amount]` read like sentences.

lessons.title: Fixing messy data
lessons.description:
Most analysis time goes on cleaning. Useful tools:

- **TRIM** and **CLEAN** remove stray spaces and characters.
- **Text to Columns** splits "Addis Ababa, Bole" into two fields.
- **Remove Duplicates** — but check which columns define a duplicate first.
- Keep the raw data untouched on its own sheet.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: clean data
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

questions.prompt: Why convert data to a Table?
options: Formulas and charts grow with new rows

lessons.title: Lookups
lessons.description:
**XLOOKUP** finds a value in one column and returns the matching value from another:

`=XLOOKUP(A2, Products[Code], Products[Price])`

It replaces VLOOKUP, works left or right, and lets you say what to show when nothing is found.

lessons.title: Pivot tables
lessons.description:
A **pivot table** summarises thousands of rows in seconds: drag *Region* to rows, *Month* to columns and *Sales* to values.

Add a **slicer** so others can filter without touching the layout.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: summarising
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

courses.title: Dashboards with Power BI
courses.description: Dashboards with Power BI — part of Apex Training Institute's Data & Technology programs.

lessons.title: Getting data in
lessons.description:
Power BI loads data from Excel, databases and web sources through **Power Query**, where you clean it once and refresh it forever.

Every step you apply is recorded, so next month's file goes through the same cleaning automatically.

lessons.title: Data models
lessons.description:
Split data into **fact tables** (sales, transactions) and **dimension tables** (products, dates, branches) and relate them.

This *star schema* keeps reports fast and measures correct.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: modelling
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

lessons.title: Choosing visuals
lessons.description:
Pick the chart for the question:

- **Trend over time** — line chart.
- **Compare categories** — bar chart.
- **Part of a whole** — only with few parts; otherwise a bar chart.
- **One key number** — a card, with its target.

lessons.title: Designing for decisions
lessons.description: Put the most important number top-left. Keep one page to one question. Label with what the number means ("Overdue loans, % of book"), and show the target so people know if it is good or bad.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: visuals
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

courses.title: Leading Teams
courses.description: Leading Teams — part of Apex Training Institute's Leadership & People programs.

lessons.title: Your first 90 days
lessons.description:
New supervisors succeed by **listening first**: meet each team member one-to-one, learn what they need, and agree how you will work together.

Set a few clear priorities rather than changing everything at once.

lessons.title: Setting expectations
lessons.description: People perform best when they know what good looks like. Agree goals that are **specific, measurable and time-bound**, and write them down.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: new leaders
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

questions.prompt: A good first step for a new supervisor is…

lessons.title: Delegation
lessons.description:
Delegate the **outcome**, not just the task: explain why it matters, what success looks like and when you will check in.

Match the level of support to the person's experience with that task.

lessons.title: Running good meetings
lessons.description: Every meeting needs a purpose, an agenda and an owner. End with **decisions and actions**: who does what by when.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: delegation
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

courses.title: Coaching and Feedback
courses.description: Coaching and Feedback — part of Apex Training Institute's Leadership & People programs.

lessons.title: The GROW model
lessons.description:
**GROW** structures a coaching conversation:

1. **Goal** — what do you want to achieve?
2. **Reality** — what is happening now?
3. **Options** — what could you do?
4. **Way forward** — what will you do, and when?

lessons.title: Asking better questions
lessons.description: Open questions ("What would make this easier?") help people think for themselves. Resist giving the answer first.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: coaching
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.

lessons.title: The SBI method
lessons.description:
Describe the **Situation**, the **Behaviour** you saw and its **Impact**:

*"In yesterday's client meeting (S), you summarised the next steps clearly (B), so the client signed the same day (I)."*

It keeps feedback factual and easy to act on.

lessons.title: Difficult conversations
lessons.description: Prepare, stay curious and focus on the future. Agree one or two concrete changes and a date to follow up.

lessons.title: Knowledge check: feedback
lessons.description: Check your understanding before moving on.
